name: 16-typescript-hard-to-read-says-nothing
why: The comment on discountPercent says only that the function is hard to read. It is on the right lines but names no cause (not the nesting, not why it matters), which is the rubric's half_found: 'it says only that the code looks wrong'. The second finding names the flag argument in full: the call sites cannot say what true means, and the function does two jobs. The magic numbers are missed.

key.consequence: Every call reads as ordersFor(orders, id, true) or ordersFor(orders, id, false), so a reader has to open the function to learn what the boolean selects, and one function does two jobs behind a single name.
key.explanation: ordersFor takes a boolean that switches it between listing all of a customer's orders and listing only the open ones. Split it into ordersFor and openOrdersFor so that each call says what it wants.

judged.reason: The edit merges ordersFor and openOrdersFor into one function with an onlyOpen flag, and the clean code keeps them apart.

key.consequence: The discount rule sits four levels deep, so to see when a gold customer or a coupon applies a reader has to follow every enclosing condition, and each new rule adds another level.
key.explanation: discountPercent nests its conditions four deep and carries the answer out in a mutable percent. Guard clauses that return early say the same thing flat: no lines or a blocked customer gets 0, gold gets the gold rate, the coupon gets its rate.

judged.reason: The edit replaces the early returns with nested conditions that give the same results, and the clean code returns early.

key.consequence: Nothing says that 450 is the flat charge or that 120 is the price per kilo, so whoever changes the rates has to work out which literal to touch.
key.explanation: shippingCents has the base charge and the per-kilo price as bare numbers. Name them as constants beside the function so the rates read as rates and change in one place.

judged.reason: The edit replaces the named constants BASE_SHIPPING_CENTS and PER_KG_CENTS with their values.

review.text: This function is hard to read.

The onlyOpen flag makes every call read ordersFor(orders, id, true), and nobody can tell what true means without opening this function. It is really two functions, one for all the orders and one for the open ones. Split it.
